flows.narrative: Two providers covering the same week ended 25 Nov diverge sharply on direction. LSEG Lipper/Reuters: global equity funds -$22.73bn (largest weekly outflow in 14 months), US equities -$30.57bn (largest since 9 Sep, with tech funds -$7.57bn), Europe +$7.29bn, EM +$971mn, bonds -$3.51bn, money-market -$49.42bn, gold -$2.14bn (largest since 25 March). EPFR/Citi (via a separately reported note): global equity funds +$63bn, US-focused funds +$23.4bn, Europe -$700mn, EM +$36.7bn (China ETFs +$28.3bn >75% of the total, Taiwan ETFs +$7bn) even as direct FII flows were net sellers of Taiwan/Korea -- a passive-ETF-buying-vs-active-selling divergence within Asia. Both agree gold saw an outflow and that money-market funds were drawn down even as equities also saw mixed flows -- an unusual 'de-risking into nothing' pattern rather than classic flight-to-safety. Crucially, all of this predates Friday 27 Nov's broad equity/metals/HK-tech rally; the next weekly print (week ending 2 Dec) would be the first to show whether flows followed price into that bounce.
